comments.author: @EarthsLastPlaces
comments.text: An island in eastern Canada where only a tiny community remains, surrounded by forests, cliffs and the Gulf of St. Lawrence, is a fascinating subject. I would love to know what keeps those few residents there.

comments.author: @antipode18
comments.text: An island 222 km long with only 175 people in one village — that's the kind of scale that breaks your brain. And the wildest part isn't the isolation, it's that this nearly empty island holds the world's best-preserved record of the first mass extinction, 440 million years old. Do the locals actually feel that deep history around them, or is it just "home" and the fossils are for the scientists?
